Article Title: Hours into probe, police yet to find motive behind Sukhbir Badal's attack
Article Text:
Hours of interrogation, motive still unclear

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked near a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded on Thursday, leaving him with injuries to his hand. One of his security personnel also sustained injuries.Badal, who has a ‘Z+’ security cover, was injured after Jaspal Singh, a man believed to be around 60-62 years old, attacked him with a ‘kirpan’ (ceremonial dagger) inside a gurdwara.Despite hours of questioning by multiple agencies, police were yet to establish a clear motive for the attack.Police said Jaspal Singh, who holds degrees in commerce and law and is a resident of Pune, was taken to the Nanded police headquarters for questioning.“Despite long hours of interrogation, the police are yet to find a concrete reason for the attack. So far, we have not found any criminal links or any such connections involving the accused in this case,” an official was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.“We are interrogating the accused, and it will go on for a long time. The former Punjab deputy CM Sukhbir Singh Badal is fine and will be discharged soon,” he added.The Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Intelligence Bureau (IB) have joined the local police in the investigation, an official told PTI.Police have registered a case against Singh at Mudkhed police station in Nanded under Sections 109(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), pertaining to attempt to murder; 118(1), relating to voluntarily causing hurt with dangerous weapons or means; and 121(2), concerning voluntarily causing grievous hurt to a public servant to deter them from performing their duty.Singh had been working as a sewadar, or volunteer, at Gurdwara Mata Sahib Devan Ji Mugat for the past two years and was living alone in Nanded, police said.Police officer Santosh Kendre, who is part of Badal’s Special Protection Unit, was injured while shielding him during the attack. Badal was walking down a flight of stairs when Singh allegedly attacked him.
Article Summary: Sikhomani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked near a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded on Thursday. Badal, who has a ‘Z+’ security cover, was injured after Jaspal Singh, a man believed to be around 60-62 years old, attacked him. One of his security personnel also sustained injuries.

Article Title: Harsimrat Kaur Badal 'deeply touched' by PM Modi's 'kind gesture' after attack on Sukhbir Badal
Article Text:
Sukhbir Badal was attacked at a gurudwara in Maharashtra's Nanded

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal on Friday said she was “deeply touched” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “kind gesture” of reaching out to enquire about the health of her husband and party chief, Sukhbir Singh Badal , who was attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded a day earlier.This marked the Badal family's first reaction to the attack on the former Punjab deputy chief minister."Truly grateful, Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji, for your personal call to inquire about Sardar Sukhbir Singh Badal ji’s health and for your good wishes for his speedy recovery following the dastardly attack on him inside a Gurudwara Sahib in Nanded, Maharashtra," Harsimrat Badal, SAD's only Lok Sabha MP, wrote on X.She also thanked the prime minister for taking immediate cognisance of the incident and directing central investigating agencies to coordinate with the state police in the probe."Your concern, support and wishes during this difficult time mean a lot to all of us in the family, our party and to the people of Punjab. I am deeply touched by your kind gesture. I am also grateful to you for taking immediate cognisance of the incident and directing central investigating agencies to coordinate with Maharashtra Police in the probe," the Bathinda MP added.On Thursday, Sukhbir Singh Badal was injured after being attacked by a kirpan-wielding assailant while leaving the Mata Sahib Devaji Gurdwara at Mudkhed in Maharashtra’s Nanded district. The assailant was arrested at the spot.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered an inquiry into the attack and spoke to Sukhbir Singh Badal over the phone. The SAD president is learnt to have told Fadnavis that he was stable, ANI reported.Earlier, Badal was also targeted in an attempted shooting at the Golden Temple in Amritsar in December 2024 while he was performing “seva”. The attacker allegedly tried to fire at him but was overpowered before he could cause any harm.The 2024 attack took place while Badal was carrying out “seva” after the Akal Takht, the highest temporal authority in Sikhism, declared him a “tankhaiya,” or guilty of religious misconduct, over decisions taken by the SAD-led Punjab government between 2007 and 2017.The SAD and BJP, which currently lead the governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, are former allies. In 2020, the SAD ended its alliance with the BJP in protest against the Centre’s contentious farm laws, which were later withdrawn.Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi last week, triggering speculation that the former allies could reunite ahead of the Punjab assembly elections early next year.
Article Summary: Harsimrat Kaur Badal said she was “deeply touched” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “kind gesture” of reaching out to enquire about the health of her husband and party chief. Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded a day earlier.

NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress is preparing to move the Supreme Court against the 20 rebel Lok Sabha MPs who merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India. A disqualification petition will be filed within 10 days, TMC sources said.TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee had met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Wednesday to reiterate his demand for a speedy decision on the disqualification petitions submitted by TMC in June. He had submitted separate letters to the speaker on each of his concerns.In one of the two letters, Banerjee stated, “More than five weeks have elapsed since filing of the petitions. To date, no notices have been issued, no hearings have been scheduled, and no procedural directions appear to have been passed. Such continued action is a matter of grave concern.” On June 19, a TMC delegation led by Banerjee had submitted the 20 disqualification petitions to Birla.He had said the urgency of the matter has been further accentuated by the decision of parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju to invite the members against whom the disqualification petitions are pending, as a separate group, to the all-party meeting held on July 19. “Such developments underscore the imperative for an expeditious determination of the petitions,” he stated to emphasise his point.

Article Title: SAD chief Sukhbir Badal attacked: 62-year-old assailant had been working at Nanded gurdwara for 2 years as 'sevadar'

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief and former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal was injured after being attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra's Nanded on Thursday. The assailant, identified as 62-year-old Jaspal Singh , had been working at the same gurdwara for the past two years as a 'sevadar' (volunteer/attendant).According to police, the attack took place when Badal was visiting Mata Sahib Gurdwara in the Hazur Sahib area. The attacker allegedly tried to stab the Akali Dal leader in the stomach, news agency IANS reported quoting sources."... Near the stairs, a 'sevadar' (volunteer/attendant) suddenly approached and attempted to attack with his 'kirpan'... Immediately following the incident, we took the attacker into custody, and interrogation is currently underway. He is approximately 60–62 years old and has been working as a 'sevadar' at the Gurudwara for about two years," Nanded Police SP Nilabh Rohan said."Initially, he himself stated that he was angry about the drug issue in Punjab... No connection to any gang has been established ... The exact reason is not yet clear. We are currently interrogating him ... The Nanded Police and the ATS are collaborating on the case," he added.Security personnel accompanying Badal intervened immediately and overpowered the attacker before he could inflict more serious injuries.Police later identified the accused as Jaspal Singh, son of Teja Singh and a resident of Solapur Bazaar in Pune. Investigators said he had been residing at Mata Sahib Gurdwara for the last two years.Badal sustained an injury to his hand and was rushed to Yasho Sai Hospital in Nanded for treatment. Officials said that he received stitches on his hand and is in stable condition.Inspector Santosh Kendre of the Maharashtra Police's Special Protection Unit (SPU), who was deployed for Badal's security, was also injured while trying to stop the attacker.The SPU is a specialised unit tasked with providing security to VVIPs during their visits and movements.Badal was accompanied by his wife, SAD MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal, during his visit to Takht Sri Hazur Sahib. Punjab security personnel and Maharashtra Police officers were also present when the attack took place.Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis has sought a detailed report from the Nanded Superintendent of Police and ordered an inquiry into the motive behind the attack. He also spoke to Badal over the phone to inquire about his condition.Police have detained the accused and launched an investigation into the circumstances that led to the attack. Security has been tightened in and around the gurdwara premises.This was not the first attack on the Akali Dal leader.In December 2024, Badal survived an assassination attempt outside the Golden Temple in Amritsar while performing 'sewadar' duties after the Akal Takht had pronounced religious punishment on him and several other party leaders over decisions taken during the SAD government's tenure between 2007 and 2017.
Article Summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal injured after being attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra's Nanded. The assailant, identified as 62-year-old Jaspal Singh, had been working at the same gurwara for the past two years as a'sevadar' (volunteer/attendant) Badal sustained an injury to his hand and was rushed to Yasho Sai Hospital.

Article Title: Parliament Monsoon Session concludes: Key takeaways from the final day of proceedings
Article Text:
Monsoon session of the Parliament concluded on Thursday

Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die

Rijiju flags low Parliament productivity

Six stanzas of Vande Mataram played in Lok Sabha

Kharge raises ‘purification’ row in Rajya Sabha

Modi and Shah present as session closes

Bills: 12 introduced, 11 passed by both Houses

NEET protests and the political battle that dominated the session

The wider legislative and political legacy

NEW DELHI: Parliament’s Monsoon Session concluded on Thursday with both Houses adjourned sine die after weeks marked by legislative business, opposition protests and repeated disruptions over the Jantar Mantar protest and other political flashpoints.The Lok Sabha’s final morning was strikingly brief. In just three minutes and 10 seconds, members assembled, all six stanzas of Vande Mataram were rendered, MPs including Prime Minister stood to attention, and Speaker Om Birla adjourned the House sine die.The closing proceedings unfolded amid familiar slogans, with the Opposition shouting “apologise, apologise” and “who ordered the lathi-charge?” as home minister Amit Shah entered. Birla also skipped his customary valedictory remarks on the House’s performance, underscoring a session dominated by disruption. Rajya Sabha witnessed Mallikarjun Kharge remarks over Haldwani 'Suddhikaran' row followed by JP Nadda's clarification and condemnation of the event.Meanwhile, in Rajya Sabha, leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge raised the Haldwani ‘suddhikaran’ row, alleging that a havan was conducted at the venue after his rally. Leader of the House JP Nadda condemned the incident and assured Kharge that the matter would be investigated.The Lok Sabha was adjourned sine die by Speaker Om Birla at 11.06 am, followed by the Rajya Sabha, bringing the 19-sitting Monsoon Session to an end. The session had been scheduled from July 20 to August 13. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju had said before the session that the government wanted the Houses to see “meaningful debate, discussion and decisions on issues of National importance”.The closing proceedings, however, came amid a continuing logjam over the opposition’s demand for a government response to the police action against students protesting the NEET controversy.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said 12 Bills were passed during the Monsoon Session, but acknowledged that parliamentary discussion remained limited. “It was a good session…we have passed 13 bills; but it was not a good session in terms of discussion,” he said. Lok Sabha productivity stood at 19%, compared with 39% in Rajya Sabha, he added. He also accused the Opposition of avoiding debate despite the government’s willingness to discuss issues.On the last day of the Monsoon Session, Lok Sabha proceedings opened with all six stanzas of Vande Mataram on Thursday, marking a first for Parliament. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and other senior leaders were present. The move followed fresh Union home ministry directions on the National Song’s protocol. During the session, Parliament also passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, providing statutory protection around national symbols.Congress president and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge used the final day to raise an alleged “purification” ritual at the Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani after his public meeting there.Kharge said, “I was in Haldwani where I made a public speech at Ramlila Maidan. Lakhs of people were there. At that time, I did not mention the name of any community or religion; I only reiterated the issues of the Govt. But after my speech, people of BJP performed a ‘havan’ there to ‘purify’ that stage...Is this the way in a democracy? How are you protecting the Constitution? I am the LoP.”Union minister JP Nadda responded that the BJP did not support such an act and said it would be investigated. “BJP does not subscribe to such activities. Never. But we will investigate this. I assure you that whatever happened there will certainly be investigated,” Nadda said, adding that he condemned the incident.PM Narendra Modi and Union HM Amit Shah were present during the closing proceedings, as the student protest controversy remained the dominant unresolved political issue. The Opposition had demanded Shah’s statement and his presence in the Houses over the police action during the July 20 march by students towards Parliament.On Wednesday, Shah said the government was prepared for a detailed discussion. “As far as the discussion is concerned, Kiren Rijiju, who is our parliamentary affairs minister, has made it very clear that the government is ready to discuss every aspect of the student protests regarding NEET,” Shah said.He added, “On my part, I have also said that I am ready to answer any question in Parliament. But they don't want the discussion to happen at all. Now let the public decide who is running away.”Rahul Gandhi rejected the offer, saying the Opposition was not interested in an “Amit Shah lecture” and questioning who ordered the use of force against protesting students.The Monsoon Session saw 12 Bills introduced, with 10 cleared by both Houses, according to PRS Legislative Research. Key legislation covered public examinations, national honour, birth and death registration, the Supreme Court, MSMEs, taxation, tribunals, cooperative development, Kerala’s name and mining.The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill received the most debate, 17 hours and 34 minutes across both Houses. Several other Bills passed with limited discussion, including four minutes each for the birth and death registration and Supreme Court judges Bills.The NEET controversy and police action against student protesters dominated the Monsoon Session, with the Opposition demanding a debate on alleged examination irregularities, education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation and accountability for the July 20 crackdown. Repeated protests led to adjournments, while the government said it was ready for discussion.The Opposition, however, linked any debate to accountability over the alleged police action. The issue remained unresolved at the session’s close. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi asked, “Who shot the students? Who gave the order to beat up the students with lathis with nails?”Beyond the NEET confrontation, the session produced a broad legislative package. Parliament cleared the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, raising the sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges other than the Chief Justice from 33 to 37; the MSME Development Amendment Bill; taxation amendments; the Tribunals Reforms Bill; the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill; the National Cooperative Development Corporation Amendment Bill and the Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill.The Kerala Bill was among the final measures passed, clearing the Lok Sabha on August 11 and the Rajya Sabha on August 12. The Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill cleared the Rajya Sabha on the final day.The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill became another major political flashpoint. Instead of being passed, it was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for detailed scrutiny amid Opposition demands that it be withdrawn.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die after weeks marked by legislative business, opposition protests and disruptions. Speaker Om Birla skipped his customary valedictory remarks on the House’s performance. Opposition shouting “apologise, apologise” and “who ordered the lathi-charge?” as home minister Amit Shah entered.

Article Title: Punjab governor recommends parole for convict Jagtar Singh Hawara in ex-CM Beant Singh assassination case
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Thursday said he has recommended parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara, who is serving a life sentence for the assassination of former chief minister Beant Singh and had sought relief to meet his ailing mother.His statement came a day after Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann urged Kataria to intervene and facilitate Hawara’s parole.Former Union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu, who is the former chief minister's grandson, had also called for Hawara to be granted parole. Beant Singh was killed in a suicide bombing in Chandigarh in 1995."His mother is unwell. We have recommended his case on humanitarian grounds,” Kataria told reporters.The governor’s intervention was required as Hawara’s parole plea is being considered in Delhi.Earlier, Mann on Wednesday backed parole for Hawara on humanitarian grounds, saying his ailing mother had a “renewed hope” of meeting her son after 31 years.The chief minister said Kataria, who is also the administrator of Chandigarh, had assured him that he would take up the matter with the Union home secretary. Mann had earlier written to Kataria, seeking 10-day parole for Hawara.Bittu, meanwhile, expressed hope that the competent authorities would consider the request expeditiously and take an appropriate decision in accordance with law.He reiterated that while his family would always honour the “supreme sacrifice” of Beant Singh, it also believed that compassion, humanity and peace should guide society forward.Last month, the Punjab and Haryana high court directed authorities at Delhi’s Mandoli prison, where Hawara is lodged, to decide his parole application in a time-bound manner after obtaining recommendations from the Chandigarh administration.Kataria, the Punjab governor, also serves as the administrator of Chandigarh.Hawara was initially sentenced to death, but the sentence was later commuted by the high court. He is serving a life sentence in connection with the blast that killed Beant Singh and 16 others.
Article Summary: Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria says he has recommended parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara. Hawara is serving a life sentence for the assassination of former chief minister Beant Singh. Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann urged Kataria to intervene and facilitate Hawara’s parole.

Article Title: Kharge claims stage 'purified' after his speech in Haldwani, govt promises action

NEW DELHI: Leader of the opposition in Rajya Sabha and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged in RS Thursday people associated with BJP "purified" the stage at Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani, two days after he made a speech there on Aug 8.Leader of the House J P Nadda said BJP did not support such activities, the incident was "painful" and action would be taken against the culprits.Raising the issue during zero hour, Kharge said, "I did not mention the name of any caste or religion, I only spoke about the problems of the people. But with great pain, I have to say that after my speech, BJP people performed a 'havan' (ritual) there and carried out purification of the stage. Is this the way democracy works? How are you protecting the Constitution?"Kharge demanded that cases be registered under Untouchability Act and those involved be arrested.Nadda said the issue shouldn't be politicised or sensationalised. "There will be a detailed investigation. Let me make it clear that BJP never subscribes to such activities. I condemn this. The incident has hurt your (Kharge) sentiments and it is a matter of regret for all of us," he said.Some MPs were heard saying that those behind the purification were protesting against the raising of slogans associated with a particular religion, because the ground also happened to be a venue for Ramlilas.Chairman C P Radhakrishnan, however, didn't allow anyone besides Kharge and Nadda to speak.Kharge said he had never told anyone he needed protection because he was a Dalit. "I have the strength to fight, and I do fight. But the purification of the stage made me feel the pain of untouchability and humiliated me," he said.Radhakrishnan said, "We all condemn untouchability. We are all purified. Those who have done this wrong will be investigated, they should be caught and punished. There are no two opinions on this."Later, calling the incident "reflective of RSS-BJP's mindset", Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said PM Narendra Modi must apologise for the caste prejudice shown towards Kharge. AICC general secretary K C Venugopal said the act went "against everything that Ambedkar and the Constitution tell us".
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge alleged people associated with BJP "purified" the stage at Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani, two days after he made a speech there on Aug 8. Kharge demanded that cases be registered under Untouchability Act and those involved be arrested.

Article Title: 'No clear information': Nepal ‘loses’ papers of centuries-old treaty defining borders with India
Article Text:
Nepali PM Balen Shah had raised up the issue of border with India, including Lipulekh.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What is the Sugauli Treaty?

NEW DELHI: Nepal has apparently lost the decades-old original of the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, a document that largely defined the Himalayan nation's boundaries with British India, its foreign minister Shisir Khanal told Parliament on Monday.Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the House of Representatives recently that while some treaty-related documents are held in the National Archives, their status as the original official documents remains unclear.“The Government of Nepal does not have clear information on whether we possess the official treaty documents. There are records showing that some documents related to certain treaties are kept at the National Archives. But we do not have clear information as to whether those are the actual official treaties,” Khanal said.He said Nepal does have documents related to the 1816 Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship with India.The disclosure comes amid renewed tensions over the Nepal-India border after India and China agreed to reopen the Lipulekh trade route. Nepal claims Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura and Kalapani as its territories, while India maintains that they are part of its territory.This becomes significant, as the dispute resurfaced recently after Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Kathmandu had raised with India concerns over alleged encroachment, including in Lipulekh. Shah said both sides had agreed to examine the issue through historians, surveyors and territorial experts and resolve it through diplomatic talks. He also called for the UK to be involved, citing its role in shaping the region's borders during the colonial era. Shah said Nepal had found that “not only had India encroached on Nepal's land, but Nepal had also encroached on India's land in multiple places.”India rejected any role for third parties, with MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal having said “there is no role for any third parties in a bilateral matter between India and Nepal.” He said nearly 98% of the boundary had been demarcated, with remaining issues including stretches affected by the shifting Gandak River and cross-border occupation or encroachment on no-man's land. India has also rejected Nepal's claims over Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura as “neither justified nor based on historical facts and evidence. ”The issue of missing treaty documents has been around for years. In 2016, when the Eminent Persons’ Group on Nepal-India Relations began discussions on reviewing or replacing the 1950 treaty, Nepal tried to locate the original but failed to find it. The government subsequently provided the Bhekh Bahadur Thapa-led committee with another copy of the treaty.The matter later prompted a parliamentary inquiry. On July 22, the Delegated Legislation and Governance Committee of Nepal's National Assembly concluded that the original copies of both the Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship could not be found in the country.The committee said it searched various locations where historical records could have been preserved, including libraries, archives and government repositories, as well as the Department of Archaeology, Narayanhiti Palace Museum, Ministry of Law and Ministry of Foreign Affairs.The matter had also come up in Parliament in 2019. Then Foreign Minister Pradeep Gyawali said the government had copies of both treaties but was unsure whether they were originals. “We have both treaties, but we have to forensically verify whether these copies are originals or not,” Gyawali had said. “We are also trying to find historical documents and maps in India and the United Kingdom.”Khanal's remarks came as he outlined a broader plan to review Nepal's existing international agreements. He said the country has 655 treaties and agreements, including 412 bilateral and 243 multilateral agreements.Of these, 55 have already been concluded or amended, while the government plans to review the remaining 600 based on their necessity and relevance. Khanal said older or inactive agreements would be reviewed, amended or renewed in coordination with the countries or international organisations concerned.“Under the general principles of international treaty law, the review, amendment, or renewal of any bilateral or multilateral treaty or agreement depends on the mutual consent and approval of the concerned state parties or relevant international organisations,” Khanal said.He added that the government would undertake the exercise with the cooperation and approval of the relevant countries and international organisations.The Sugauli Treaty was agreed between Nepal and the British East India Company after the Anglo-Nepalese War. It was signed in December 1815 and ratified in March 1816, with the agreement establishing the basis for Nepal's territorial boundary with British India.The treaty required Nepal to cede significant territories to the East India Company and renounce claims to lands west of the Kali River, while also setting out provisions governing relations between Nepal and the Company.
Article Summary: Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the House of Representatives that while some treaty-related documents are held in the National Archives, their status as the original official documents remains unclear. The disclosure comes amid renewed tensions over the Nepal-India border after India and China agreed to reopen the Lipulekh trade route.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked Union Public Service Commission to defer the selection of a panel of three officers from which the Odisha govt was to choose the successor of present DGP Y B Khurania, who retires on Aug 16.Appearing for applicant Jayant Das, senior advocate P Chidambaram told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that a certain ADGP was hurriedly promoted to DGP rank and included in the panel of names sent by Odisha govt to UPSC , which was against the DGP selection procedure laid down by SC in the two decade-old Prakash Singh judgement.When amicus curiae and senior advocate Raju Ramachandran said the matter required consideration, Odisha advocate general Pitambara Acharya said the state had followed Prakash Singh guidelines scrupulously and sent names of 11 DGP-rank police officers to UPSC for preparation of a panel of three-most suitable officers.“The complainant has seven criminal cases pending against him and is a habitual offender. Article Title: Real 'Sena' battle: 'Sin' of defection should not be rewarded, Uddhav camp tells SC
Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray addresses a press conference, at Bandra, in Mumbai. (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: The Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena (UBT) on Thursday told the Supreme Court that constitutional provisions cannot be interpreted in a way that encourages the very conduct the anti-defection law was enacted to prevent. Appearing before a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant during the fifth day of hearings on the party symbol dispute, senior advocate Kapil Sibal argued that the Constitution should not be read in a manner that rewards defections and weakens democratic safeguards.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing petitions filed by the Thackeray faction challenging the Election Commission's decision to recognise the Eknath Shinde-led faction as the real Shiv Sena and allot it the party's name and the 'bow and arrow' symbol."You can't interpret the provisions of the Constitution to give encouragement to the very sin which the anti-defection law sought to prevent," Sibal told the bench.Sibal argued that the legal test for disqualification is fundamentally different from the test for determining whether a political party has split. "Split is completely different, and disqualification is completely different," he said, adding that subsequent events may be relevant in disqualification proceedings but not when deciding whether a split had occurred.He told the court that the case presented an opportunity to lay down the law for the future of Indian democracy.Calling the situation a "very sad state of affairs", Sibal said governments often ensure that disqualification proceedings remain undecided.When he argued that the burden of preserving democracy rested on the judiciary, the bench responded that it was a "collective responsibility". "We are conscious of our role. The Constitution is lived by the people," the bench observed.The Chief Justice added, "Let us not underestimate our other institutions. They are also quite committed."Sibal replied that while Parliament could continue enacting laws, it was ultimately the Supreme Court that had the authority to interpret and test those laws against the Constitution.The hearing has been adjourned and will continue on 18 August.During Wednesday's proceedings, the Supreme Court had observed that it would first have to determine whether a split had occurred within the Shiv Sena, noting that a division could originate in the legislature party and later spread through the party organisation and primary membership.Responding to that observation, Sibal argued that a split in the legislature party could not by itself amount to a split in the political party. "As a proposition of law, a split in the political party can never arise merely from a split in the legislature party. That has been decided by the Constitution Bench (in a judgment)," he said.He also questioned the Election Commission's approach in deciding whether there was a genuine dispute within the Shiv Sena and whether the faction approaching it had exhausted the internal remedies available under the party constitution. Sibal challenged the Commission's assessment of the Shiv Sena's organisational structure, including the powers of the party chief and the process for appointing organisational office-bearers.The bench is hearing two petitions filed by the Thackeray faction in 2024 challenging the Election Commission's order allotting the 'bow and arrow' symbol to the Eknath Shinde-led faction and the Commission's 17 February 2023 decision recognising it as the original Shiv Sena.
Article Summary: The Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena (UBT) told the Supreme Court that constitutional provisions cannot be interpreted in a way that encourages the very conduct the anti-defection law was enacted to prevent. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal argued that the Constitution should not be read in a manner that rewards defections and weakens democratic safeguards.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday said the party's job was to make India “express itself” and claimed the BJP-led government was increasingly unsettled by people's voices. Speaking at the Ratchnatmak Congress National Convention, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha also took several digs at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, home minister Amit Shah and the RSS.“Our job is very simple and we can drive them crazy...I am telling you, (PM) Narendra Modi does not sleep at night,” Rahul said. Referring to Shah, he added, “You saw (HM) Amit Shah, what did they used to call him? Chanakya? And Sardar Patel... Where has he disappeared? He could not enter Parliament House... Why? Because, for the first time, they are feeling India’s expression...”Gandhi said the Congress would seek to challenge what he described as the BJP's attempt to impose a particular political order on the country.“What was happening at Jantar Mantar is that students want to express themselves. They are in pain, and they want to express themselves, and the government says no.We are going to create order at Jantar Mantar. You cannot express yourselves,” he said.“So their job and their political philosophy is to impose an order on India, an order that benefits them and certain other people. And our job is to make India express itself and break that order,” Gandhi added.He was referring to the protests at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak. The CJP-led protest ended after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister, while opposition parties in Parliament demanded a statement from Home Minister Amit Shah on the alleged police action against protesters.Gandhi also attacked the RSS, saying the organisation did not understand contemporary India. “I can understand if you are fighting the British Empire and suddenly you say, I'm feeling a bit scared. But you're fighting a bunch of jokers. How can you feel scared? You're literally fighting a bunch of jokers, clowns who have no idea about our philosophy, no idea about our history. I can naturally say this about my friends in the RSS. It's obvious to me,” he said.“In fact, it's obvious to most people that these people have no understanding of India. Why? Because somebody who cannot connect with India as it is today cannot understand India. To understand India, you can't understand India 3,000 years ago. You have to understand it today, right now. And to understand it today, the only way to understand it today is to understand its expression,” he added.The LoP also criticised the government's foreign policy, referring to the war in Iran and India's ties with the US, Russia and Iran.“War broke out in Iran. For India—had it recognized its own strength and had its leader been someone like Indira Gandhi—this presented the greatest opportunity in the world,” he said.“What kind of opportunity? Iran was our old friend, America was our friend, and Russia was our friend. We could have stepped up, become relevant, and leveraged these friendships. But what actually happened? Nothing of the sort. Instead, Pakistan stepped in and took our place; Pakistan became the mediator, while India and Modi-ji simply looked on,” Gandhi claimed.He also alleged that the government was suppressing information about India's border situation with China.“Rajnath Singh, Amit Shah, and Narendra Modi have been completely deflated. They are calling up all the media editors, telling them, ‘Don't publish this in your newspapers; suppress the story.’ They are causing direct harm to the country without a second thought,” he alleged.Gandhi further referred to the government's response after the Galwan clash and claimed that India's position had weakened its negotiations with China.“After the Galwan incident, the Prime Minister held a meeting—a Zoom call. He stated that China hadn't taken a single inch of Indian territory. The Army said that our land had been taken. Just think about the message sent to China: Chinese negotiators asked our negotiators, ‘What nonsense are you talking about? Your own Prime Minister said no land was lost.’”He alleged that the government's foreign-policy decisions were ultimately driven by political funding, adding, “And they did all of this solely to finance their political structure, to secure funds from Adani ji.”Rahul also criticised what he described as the government's approach to diplomacy, saying foreign policy could not be reduced to personal relationships between leaders.“I don't know where it came from; this idea got into their heads. I don't know who put it there or where it came from, the idea that foreign policy means hugging politicians,” he said.Recalling an incident from his childhood involving his grandmother and former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi said she had returned from an official dinner in the US and told his mother, Sonia Gandhi, that “these Americans take me for a complete fool.”Gandhi said Indira Gandhi had noticed that then-US First Lady Nancy Reagan was wearing a dress of the same colour as her sari.“You aren't just visiting a friend's house. In this role, the Prime Minister of India doesn't engage in mere friendship. They have no interest in friendship; their job is to protect the country,” he said.Read more: Rahul mocks PM; another Congress leader takes Meloni swipe
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi says the party's job is to make India 'express itself' Gandhi also takes several digs at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, home minister Amit Shah and the RSS. NEW DELHI: The West Bengal government on Thursday withdrew the Banga Bibhushan award from BJP Rajya Sabha member Ananta Maharaj over his alleged derogatory comment against Netaji.Banga Bibhushan is one of West Bengal’s highest civilian honours, awarded by the state government to eminent personalities for outstanding contributions in fields such as art, culture, literature, social service and other areas. A police officer from Badal’s security team intervened and pushed the gunman’s hand upward, causing the bullet to miss Badal.A sewadar also helped overpower Chaura. Badal was unharmed in the incident.At the time, Badal was seated at the Golden Temple entrance in a blue sewadar uniform as part of the tankhah religious punishment imposed by the Akal Takht over alleged religious misconduct during his father Parkash Singh Badal’s tenure as Punjab chief minister from 2007 to 2017.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inquired about Badal's health in a phone conversation with his wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal, according to sources. Badal suffered hand injuries and his security personnel was injured. One person has been detained in connection with the incident.

Article Title: 'Bid to weaken stir': Students accuse Jharkhand govt of withholding Devendra Mahto's health details
Article Text:
Jharkhand chief minister Raghubar Das on Thursday visited Mahto at the hospital.

Students allege govt hiding Mahto’s health details

Raghubar Das meets Mahto

Jharkhand protest enters 20th day

NEW DELHI: Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who is on an indefinite hunger strike over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations, remains hospitalised at Sadar Hospital in Ranchi, with protesting students alleging that the state government is withholding information about his health to weaken their agitation.Meanwhile, former Jharkhand chief minister Raghubar Das on Thursday visited Mahto at the hospital and enquired about his health.Mahto has been on hunger strike for 11 days and is undergoing treatment after he was injured during a police lathi-charge on August 10. The wider protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants entered its 20th day on Thursday, with students continuing their agitation at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.The protesting students have alleged that the government is not allowing them to meet Mahto at the hospital and is withholding details about his health.Mahto was moved to Sadar Hospital by the administration late Monday evening after police used force to disperse thousands of aspirants who had marched towards the state assembly.In a post on X, Mahto said: "Former Chief Minister of Jharkhand Raghubar Das ji reached the hospital and inquired about my well-being, while also assuring support for our movement."Das had on Wednesday threatened to go on a hunger strike if the demand for a CBI probe was not fulfilled within a week.He has also sought compensation of Rs 1 crore each for the families of 19 people who died during the 2024 excise constable physical examination.The BJP has accused the Hemant Soren government of suppressing the student movement, while the Congress has accused the saffron party of politicising the agitation and alleged that it brought workers from outside Jharkhand to disrupt the protests.On Tuesday, in a message shared on social media, Mahto said "My body is undergoing treatment in the hospital bed, but my soul and resolve are at the Satyagraha site where students and youth are engaged in a just struggle for their future. The indefinite hunger strike continues on its 11th day in Sadar Hospital."Mahto has also sought permission from the hospital authorities to return to the protest site. In a handwritten application to the Civil Surgeon, he said being separated from the protesting students was causing him greater distress than his physical ailments.He cited his responsibility towards thousands of students protesting against alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations and sought permission to rejoin them.The protesters have been demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process. They have alleged that their demands have not been fully accepted by the state government.The students’ agitation over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations entered its 20th day on Thursday. The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch has been demonstrating at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, demanding greater transparency in recruitment examinations, cancellation of several tests and an independent probe by the CBI or a panel of retired judges from outside Jharkhand.Tensions escalated on Monday when JPSC and JSSC aspirants marched towards the state assembly. Police used batons, water cannons and tear gas to disperse the protesters.Mahto was among those taken to hospital after the confrontation. He later sought permission to leave the hospital and return to the protest site, saying his presence with the students was important to the movement.The ABVP has announced protests at more than 1,200 universities over the issue. Its leaders have also questioned the credibility of the state-appointed SIT into the alleged examination irregularities, citing repeated changes in its composition.The protesters have so far refused to call off the agitation, maintaining that they will continue the movement until their demands are addressed.
Article Summary: Devendra Nath Mahto remains hospitalised at Sadar Hospital in Ranchi. Former Jharkhand chief minister Raghubar Das on Thursday visited Mahto. Mahto has been on hunger strike for 11 days and is undergoing treatment after he was injured during a police lathi-charge.

Article Title: Parliament Monsoon Session ends amid disruptions; Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die
Article Text:
File photo: Proceedings in the Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament, in New Delhi.

Rijiju says session successful in business, but debate fell short

Rajya Sabha skips question hour, passes Mines and Minerals Bill

Lok Sabha ends amid opposition protests

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Monsoon Session of Parliament ended on Thursday with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha being adjourned sine die amid repeated disruptions and political confrontations between the government and Opposition.The session, which began on July 20, witnessed protests inside and outside the Houses over several issues, while Parliament also passed a number of legislations.Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the Monsoon Session was successful in terms of legislative business but fell short on debate and discussion. He said Parliament passed 12 Bills during the session, but productivity remained low amid repeated disruptions."In terms of business, it was a very successful session; we passed a total of 12 bills. However, from the perspective of debate and discussion, it was not as successful," Rijiju said.He said the Lok Sabha recorded 19 per cent productivity against the total time allotted, while productivity in the Rajya Sabha stood at 39 per cent. Rijiju attributed the lower productivity largely to disruptions by Opposition parties, while noting that NDA members and MPs from some Opposition parties participated in debates.Rijiju said only one Bill in the Lok Sabha — the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, dealing with paper leaks and unfair means in examinations — underwent a full discussion. The legislation was also discussed in the Rajya Sabha.He criticised the Opposition for not allowing debates to proceed, saying the government was ready to provide answers to questions raised by Opposition MPs. "This is not healthy for the parliamentary democracy," Rijiju said.He also accused Congress MPs of focusing on slogans, placards and protests instead of parliamentary debate, and said he hoped there would be a change before the Winter Session."In the Lok Sabha, 11 bills were passed without discussion, while one underwent discussion," Rijiju said, adding that the concerned Bill was fully discussed in the Rajya Sabha.The Rajya Sabha was adjourned sine die after chairman C P Radhakrishnan highlighted the performance of the House during the session.Deviating from the normal pre-lunch schedule on the final day, the Upper House dispensed with the Zero Hour and Question Hour and took up the Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill. The legislation was subsequently passed by a voice vote.The Rajya Sabha had witnessed repeated disruptions during the session over issues including police action against students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak and allegations concerning the theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.The House also witnessed a confrontation between leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge and the government over an alleged 'Shuddhikaran' or purification ritual at a stage in Haldwani after Kharge addressed a Congress rally there on August 8.Kharge raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha, saying he had spoken about people's problems and had not mentioned any community or religion during his speech.“But after my speech, people associated with the BJP carried out a 'purification' ritual of that stage,” Kharge said, questioning whether such an incident was appropriate in a democracy.Leader of the House JP Nadda said the BJP did not support such activities and assured the House that the allegation would be investigated.“What Kharge ji has said is truly a matter of concern—not just for the Congress party, but for all of us,” Nadda said. “I want to make it absolutely clear that the BJP does not subscribe to such activities.”Chairman C P Radhakrishnan said untouchability was condemned by all members and asked the government to investigate the allegation and punish those responsible if it was found to be true.The Lok Sabha was also adjourned sine die soon after proceedings began on the final day, following the traditional playing of Vande Mataram.Proceedings were disrupted by Opposition MPs amid sloganeering, with political tensions also spilling into the Parliament complex.BJP and opposition held counter-protests at the Makar Dwar steps, with the BJP protesting against Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi over the Congress' position on the ongoing protests in Jharkhand.Opposition MPs, meanwhile, raised demands for the Union Home Minister to make a statement in the House and for the Prime Minister to respond to issues raised by them.Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi accused the ruling party of preventing Parliament from functioning.“It is the ruling party itself that is preventing Parliament from functioning,” he said, arguing that the Opposition had been seeking discussions and responses from the government on issues including the Public Examinations Amendment Act.Union minister Manohar Lal Khattar rejected the opposition's allegations and said Parliament could not function without discussion.“The Lok Sabha is a forum for discussion. There is no point in proceeding without discussion,” Khattar said. He added that the House was a platform for representatives from across the country and “does not belong to any single individual”.The session ended after weeks of political confrontation, with disruptions remaining a prominent feature of proceedings in both Houses.
Article Summary: The Monsoon Session of Parliament ended on Thursday with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha being adjourned sine die. The session, which began on July 20, witnessed protests inside and outside the Houses over several issues. Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the session was successful in terms of business but fell short on debate and discussion.

Article Title: Vande Mataram row: Tamil Thaai Vazhthu to be first song at state official events
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu mandates Tamil Thaai Vazhthu as first song at official events

The Tamil Nadu government has issued an order making ‘Tamil Thaai Vazhthu’, the state song, the first song to be rendered at all official events.The order applies to public, educational and government functions and mandates that attendees stand while the song is being played, with an exemption for persons with disabilities.The government order, issued by chief secretary M Sai Kumar on Wednesday, follows a unanimous resolution passed by the Tamil Nadu Assembly on August 10. It applies to all educational institutions, universities, government offices and public sector undertakings.The order also referred to the resolution piloted by chief minister C Joseph Vijay, stating that the “Assembly proudly records that Tamil is the ancient classical language of the world and Tamil civilisation is one of the oldest cultural traditions in the world.”Tamil Thaai Vazhthu was officially accorded the status of Tamil Nadu’s State Song on December 12, 2021, with its rendition made mandatory before programmes at educational institutions, universities, government offices, public sector undertakings and other public institutions in the state.The song is taken from Manonmaniam, a play written by Manonmaniam Sundaranar in 1891. It has been sung at the beginning of government functions since November 23, 1970, and was formally recognised as the state song in December 2021.The latest mandate comes amid observations by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs in a July 9 letter on the rendition of the State Song, including guidance on the sequence of songs and a reference to Vande Mataram President Droupadi Murmu has given her assent to the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, granting Vande Mataram, India’s national song, the same statutory protection as the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana.The legislation amends the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971. Parliament passed the Bill last month, and with the President’s assent, the amendments have now come into force as law.
Article Summary: Tamil Thaai Vazhthu was officially accorded the status of Tamil Nadu’s State Song on December 12, 2021. It has been sung at the beginning of government functions since November 23, 1970, and was formally recognised as the state song in December 2021.

Article Title: Al-Qaida offshoot AQIS behind Red Fort blast in 2025: UNSC report confirms
Article Text:
11 people were killed in the blast on November 10, 2025

NEW DELHI: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has officially attributed the November 2025 blast near Delhi’s iconic Red Fort to Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS), according to the 38th report of its Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team.The attack on November 10 last year claimed 11 lives."Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS, not listed) continued to evolve from a fragmented group into a regional terrorist entity; it established logistics and financial networks, working in decentralised, small, scattered cells instead of large units. The attack in November 2025 on the Red Fort in Delhi was officially attributed to AQIS," the report, published on August 10, stated.The assessment marks a significant shift in the attribution of the Red Fort attack, which had earlier been linked to the Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM).The report noted that one member state had attributed a series of attacks to JeM and also linked the group to the Red Fort blast.The explosion occurred around 7 pm when a moving Hyundai i20 erupted in flames near the iconic monument.Investigators identified Umar-e-Nabi as the driver of the car and suspect him of carrying out the attack as a suicide bomber.Read also: Red Fort blast: 7,500-page NIA charge sheet alleges ‘Operation Heavenly Hind’ to overthrow govt Launched in 2014, AQIS is a regional affiliate of Al-Qaida.The group was formed to expand the organisation’s activities across South Asia, including India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and parts of Afghanistan.Meanwhile, the latest UNSC assessment also flagged broader concerns over the activities and capabilities of Al-Qaida and Islamic State (ISIL/Da’esh) affiliates.The report noted that Al-Qaida and ISIL had for years shown interest in developing chemical and biological weapons but had so far failed to overcome the technical challenges involved. It also highlighted the widespread circulation of instructions on producing such agents in online terrorist communities.The report cited material published by ISIL’s English-language Invade magazine in February that included instructions related to botulinum toxin and cyanide. It also noted that ISIL-K had shown particular interest in ricin and circulated instructions on developing the toxin over the previous 12 months.
Article Summary: The United Nations Security Council has officially attributed the November 2025 blast near Delhi’s iconic Red Fort to Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) The assessment marks a significant shift in the attribution of the Red Fort attack, which had earlier been linked to the Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM)

Article Title: 'Soon in a trash can': Iran mocks Trump's secret getaway via catering truck
Article Text:
Photo mocking Trump posted on X by Iran embassy in South Africa

Iranian state media has mocked US President Donald Trump over the secret aircraft switch that took place during his departure from Turkey last month, portraying the episode as evidence of Washington's fear of Iran's military capabilities.A presenter on Iranian state television described the incident as a new “scandal” for Trump and said it had become a source of humiliation for the US president. The comments came after new details emerged about the security operation during Trump's return from the Nato summit in Ankara.The operation was prompted by what US officials described as a credible threat that the presidential aircraft could be targeted by a shoulder-fired missile. Trump was secretly moved from Air Force One to a smaller C-32A government jet, while the larger presidential aircraft left separately with senior administration officials, staff and journalists on board.The New York Times had reported that US intelligence also found that Iranian operatives knew where Trump was staying in Ankara, including the floor of his hotel. Tehran has not officially commented on those allegations or the aircraft switch.The episode quickly became material for Iranian propaganda and social media. Iran's embassy in South Africa posted a meme showing Trump inside a catering box filled with food, alongside a warning that he would “be hidden in a trash can before long”.In a follow up post Iran claimed that, “The one they claimed was hiding in a bunker was martyred in his office. Yet the one who boasted about his massive warships and advanced B-2 bombers ended up fleeing in a food truck.”The catering truck was reportedly used to conceal Trump and a small group of aides as they moved from the presidential aircraft to the smaller jet on July 8.Iranian state media also pointed to the broader symbolism of the incident, with a television presenter arguing that the extraordinary security measures demonstrated the reach of Iran's military power. Tehran has previously rejected US allegations that it was involved in plots against Trump.
Article Summary: Iranian state media has mocked US President Donald Trump over the secret aircraft switch that took place during his departure from Turkey last month. The episode was prompted by what US officials described as a credible threat that the presidential aircraft could be targeted by a shoulder-fired missile. Trump was secretly moved from Air Force One to a smaller C-32A government jet.

Article Title: Engulfed in flames, smoke: 2 killed as Russia hits passenger train with 340 onboard, says Zelenskyy
Article Text:
Train on fire (Video shared by Zelenskyy on X)

Ukraine’s drones hit major Russian refinery

A passenger train with 340 people onboard was attacked in Ukraine's Odesa region on Thursday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed, saying the train's driver and his assistant were killed in the strike.Zelenskyy said a Russian drone struck the locomotive of the passenger train. He said the target was a civilian train and that the operator of the drone could not have been unaware of its nature. The claims have not been independently verified.“Today in the Odesa region, the Russians once again destroyed an ordinary passenger train locomotive with a jet-powered drone. There were 340 people on the train,” Zelenskyy said in a post on X.“As of now, unfortunately, we know that the locomotive engineer and his assistant were killed in the strike,” he added, offering condolences to their families.Zelenskyy also said Russian forces carried out strikes across 11 Ukrainian regions overnight, using more than 130 attack drones.He called for greater air defence support for Ukraine and increased international pressure on Russia, saying stronger action was needed to stop the war.The attack comes amid continued Russian drone and missile strikes across Ukraine, with Odesa and its surrounding region frequently targeted.As the attacks continue from both sides, Ukrainian forces were later reported to have struck the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining and petrochemical complex in Russia’s Bashkortostan overnight, causing a fire, Ukraine’s General Staff said. The facility, located about 1,300 km from Ukraine’s border, is one of Russia’s largest oil refineries and petrochemical complexes.The General Staff said the plant can process up to 74 million barrels of oil annually, producing gasoline, diesel and other petroleum products. “The complex is one of Russia’s largest oil refining and petrochemical facilities,” it said.Bashkortostan Governor Radiy Khabirov said a drone attack wounded two civilians and started a fire in an industrial zone in Salavat. The strike was the fourth major Ukrainian attack on Russian energy infrastructure in three days, according to AP.
Article Summary: Ukraine’s drones hit major Russian refinery in Bashkortostan. A passenger train with 340 people onboard was attacked in Ukraine's Odesa region. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the train's driver and his assistant were killed in the strike.

Article Title: F-16 fighter jet crashes in Turkey during training flight, pilot safe
