Article Title: Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp, Walt Nauta: 3 aides were allowed with Trump when he was moved into a catering truck during Turkey emergency
Article Text:
Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp and Walt Nauta are the closest aides allowed inside the catering truck that hid President Donald Trump in Turkey.

Who is Dan Scavino?

Who is Natalie Harp?

Who is Walt Nauta?

No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Apart from some low-ranking aides, only three individuals were allowed inside the truck, as they are believed to be the closest to the president: Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations. Washington Post reported that neither Marco Rubio nor Pete Hegseth nor Stephen Miller were allowed inside the truck that took TrumpThe catering truck moved under concealment from the Air Force One aircraft to a smaller Air Force C-32A before flying to Britain separately.Dan Scavino has been serving as the White House deputy chief of staff in the second Trump administration but his history with Trump dates back to 1992, when he worked as a caddie at a New York country club that Trump later purchased and turned into Trump National Golf Club Westchester. After graduating from college, Scavino worked his way up to become the golf club's general manager.He joined Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and went on to serve throughout the entire first Trump administration as White House Director of Social Media and later Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications.During that time, he was particularly known for managing Trump's personal social media presence and online strategy. He remained a central advisor at Mar-a-Lago following the 2020 election, worked as a senior official on the 2024 campaign, and returned to senior White House leadership upon Trump taking office again in 2025.Natalie Harp is an American political aide and former television presenter who serves as Executive Assistant to the President in Donald Trump's second White House administration. She is the one who handles the president's daily schedule and is always spotted with him. Known colloquially among campaign staffers and media outlets as Trump's "human printer," Harp earned a reputation for constantly accompanying him with a portable printer to feed him printed news articles, polls, and favorable commentary. In her role as executive assistant, she remains a member of his inner circle, assisting with his daily schedule and managing dictation for his social media accounts.Walt Nauta is a close political aide to Donald Trump and currently serves in his second White House administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Director of Oval Office Operations. Nauta spent 20 years in the U.S. Navy, reaching the rank of Senior Chief Petty Officer. During his military career, he was assigned to the Presidential Food Service and eventually became a White House valet during Trump's first presidency. In that role, he acted as a personal assistant and "body man," handling day-to-day tasks like fetching beverages and managing travel details.After Trump left office in 2021, Nauta retired from the Navy and joined Trump's personal staff at Mar-a-Lago, continuing to work as his primary executive assistant and political aide. He later drew widespread national attention when he was indicted alongside Trump in June 2023 in the federal classified documents case, where prosecutors accused him of helping move and conceal boxes of sensitive materials.
Article Summary: No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations, are believed to be the closest aides to the president.

Article Title: Thailand visit, Suu Kyi access: Can Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing win political legitimacy?
Article Text:
Min Aung Hlaing in Thailand; Aung San Suu Kyi with ICRC official

Min Aung Hlaing's ascent to power

Significance of Aung San Suu Kyi

Why Thailand visit matters for Min Aung Hlaing - and how Bangkok differs from ASEAN

Can regional engagement help Min Aung Hlaing’s legitimacy push?

Min Aung Hlaing’s continuing legitimacy challenge

Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week, in a trip that carried significance beyond routine diplomacy. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency.That visit to Thailand coincided with another significant development in Myanmar. Aung San Suu Kyi , the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor. On August 3, Suu Kyi met Arnaud de Baecque, the International Committee of the Red Cross' (ICRC) resident representative in her country.Naypyidaw also released photographs of the meeting—the first official images of the former State Counsellor in years.Was the close timing of the two developments just a coincidence? For Min Aung Hlaing, who came to power by overthrowing an elected government rather than through the ballot box, both developments could be part of a broader effort to build political legitimacy and gain wider international acceptance.During his visit to Thailand, the 70-year-old former military leader sought to reassure his host, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, that Myanmar was “returning to democracy.”"Myanmar has now re-established itself on the path to democracy and is moving toward a better future," Min Aung Hlaing told Charnvirakul.The remarks stood in sharp contrast to the circumstances of his rise to the presidency. His claim that Myanmar is on a “democratic path” also comes against the backdrop of a bloody civil war triggered by the coup that brought him to power.According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent organisation that documents arrests and casualties linked to the Myanmar civil war, more than 8,200 civilians had been killed and 31,645 people arrested by the regime's security forces as of August 5.Besides, the parliamentary elections under Min Aung Hlaing in late 2025 and early 2026 were also widely criticised as “neither free nor fair” as the army-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party swept the elections, winning 232 of the 263 contested seats in the lower house and 109 of 157 seats in the upper house. Ahead of the presidential election in April—Myanmar's first since 2018—he resigned from the military and was subsequently elected president.However, his transition to the presidency did little to ease international scepticism. Major democracies withheld congratulations following his victory.For Myanmar, Aung San Suu Kyi’s significance extends beyond her role as the head of the country’s first democratically elected civilian government in 50 years and the military’s toppling of her administration.For many inside and outside Myanmar, the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize laureate remains the country's most recognisable symbol of democratic rule and civilian legitimacy.In 2022, Suu Kyi was sentenced to 33 years in prison on a series of charges that her supporters and rights groups described as “politically motivated” and intended to prevent her return to politics. Later, her sentence was reduced to 27 years and, in April, to 18 years, while she was transferred to house arrest.Against this backdrop, the meeting with the ICRC representative was significant because it marked the first confirmed contact between Suu Kyi, 81, and an independent international organisation since her house arrest. It was also her first confirmed communication with the outside world since she wrote a letter to her son from prison in early 2024.Sreeparna Banerjee, an Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF), agreed that both developments could be seen as part of Myanmar’s broader effort to “manage its international image,” but said it cannot be assumed that the moves were directly linked.“The timing is noteworthy, but it would be difficult to establish a direct connection between the two developments at this stage… Access to Aung San Suu Kyi after a prolonged period of isolation could signal some limited openness, while Min Aung Hlaing’s high-profile visit to Thailand demonstrates Myanmar’s attempt to expand diplomatic engagement,” Banerjee, whose work focuses on Myanmar and Thailand, told The Times of India.For Min Aung Hlaing, the bigger challenge remains turning such diplomatic engagement into wider political legitimacy and international acceptance.According to Banerjee, the visit was important for Min Aung Hlaing because it offered him a degree of political normalisation.“Being received at the highest level by an ASEAN neighbour allows him to project the image of a leader whose government is once again engaging with the region rather than remaining diplomatically isolated,” she said.Significantly, while Thailand and Myanmar are both ASEAN member states, Bangkok’s approach towards Naypyidaw differs from that of the rest of the 11-nation bloc of Southeast Asian states.Thailand has continued to engage with Myanmar despite ASEAN barring Min Aung Hlaing from its top-level meetings over the non-implementation of the Five-Point Consensus agreed with the grouping after he seized power.On this, Banerjee observed that the real value of Bangkok’s “bridge” diplomacy — acting as a bridge between Myanmar and ASEAN — would depend on whether Thailand can use it to encourage some meaningful progress on the Five-Point Consensus.Additionally, ASEAN is yet to recognise the results of Myanmar’s 2025–26 parliamentary elections. The bloc has also repeatedly called for Suu Kyi’s unconditional release, renewing the demand after her meeting with the ICRC official. The regime rebuffed this call too.For its part, Thailand has described its approach vis-à-vis Myanmar as one of “calibrated re-engagement” aimed at keeping dialogue open while responding to “realities on the ground.” Bangkok has also argued that Myanmar is essential to ASEAN unity and regional stability, provided it remains peaceful and stable.In addition to being barred from top-level ASEAN summits, Min Aung Hlaing faces Western sanctions over his role in toppling Suu Kyi’s government, the subsequent civil war, and the alleged persecution of the Rohingya minority in the Rakhine province.The Thailand visit was his fourth overseas trip since becoming president, following visits to India, China, and Laos. India was the only democratic country among the four destinations, underscoring the limited engagement he has so far had with democratic governments.Despite this, and close ties with Russia, he has remained largely isolated internationally.So, can his engagement with Thailand and his wider regional outreach — help him in his bid for greater international recognition and acceptance?Sreeparna Banerjee, the ORF Associate Fellow, suggested that even regional acceptance remains uncertain at this stage, despite such engagement being an important part of Myanmar’s quest for political legitimacy.“Naypyidaw appears determined to engage on its own terms rather than fully follow the ASEAN framework. Thailand's outreach may create space for dialogue, but whether this translates into wider regional acceptance remains uncertain,” she explained.She also highlighted that uncertainty over Myanmar’s regional acceptance stems in part from the fact that Singapore will take over the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027. The city-state has repeatedly called for full implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.This underscores the scale of the challenge facing Min Aung Hlaing in his bid for wider acceptance.For a leader who rises to power as Min Aung Hlaing did, securing international recognition is likely to remain a gradual and difficult process.The regime’s refusal to release Suu Kyi, a global icon, further complicates that effort.Engagement with neighbouring countries can provide an important opening, but broader recognition often depends on how other governments assess the resulting political situation. Yet for Min Aung Hlaing, this remains the only option to secure recognition.For now, engagement with Thailand may offer Min Aung Hlaing some diplomatic space, but whether it can translate into legitimacy for him remains uncertain.
Article Summary: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency. Aung San Suu Kyi, the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor.

Article Title: US Department of Labor official Anthony D’Esposito slams H-1B program, but says the real people to blame are not workers on H-1B visas, but federal government as ...
Article Text:
Fraud within the H-1B visa program: Investigation underway

Increasing political pressure

H-1B visa workers would be required to leave US immediately

Anthony D’Esposito, Inspector General at the Department of Labour has launched a sweeping investigation into fraud within the H-1B visa program, according to a report by Breitbart. D’Esposito has described the program as a ‘criminal enterprise’ which stretches beyond the borders of the US. He also said that the criminal networks are selling the white-collar jobs of Americans through the program which now keeps at least 1 million foreign workers in positions sought by US graduates. Along with this, D’Esposito also stressed that the real blame lies not with the individual H-1B workers but with the federal government and employers.“The fact is the real people to blame are the federal government — because the federal government allowed it to go unchecked — and the companies who are taking away jobs from the very people who they need to buy their product in order for them to stay in business… So I don’t think that the individuals in every case are really the bad guys. I think that they are being utilized as pawns in a seriously dangerous operation.”The probe initiated by D’Esposito is part of vice president JD Vance’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud which started in July and has already managed to uncover firearms and other crimes during search warrants in multiple states.D’Esposito said oversight of visa programs has historically been minimal, allowing companies to rely heavily on foreign labor and undercut American workers.The H‑1B program was intended to help companies fill unique skill gaps temporarily, but D’Esposito argued many firms now use it to staff entire workforces. He noted that H‑1B workers often earn 25–30% less than Americans, and when visas expire, some are pressured into illegal work at exploitative wages.Lawmakers and investors are increasingly critical of the program’s impact on U.S. workers, with recent data showing high underemployment among new graduates. D’Esposito emphasised that the investigation is focused on protecting the labor market, not targeting migrants, and vowed to pursue every lead to expose fraud and restore fairness in employment.In related news, a recent online report revealed that a proposed rule by the US government could remove the 60-day grace period currently available to H-1B visa holders and several other temporary workers after they lose their jobs. If the proposal is approved, affected workers may have to leave the United States immediately and would generally not be able to change their immigration status or switch employers from within the country unless the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) decides to forgive the lapse in status. According to a Bloomberg report, the proposal is currently under review.The proposal is currently being reviewed by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB). Once the review is complete, it will be published in the Federal Register for a public comment period of 30 to 60 days before any final decision is made.If the rule is finalized, foreign workers whose employment ends before their visa period expires would generally no longer be considered to be maintaining lawful status. As a result, they would be required to leave the US immediately and would not be allowed to change employers or switch to another visa category while remaining in the country, unless USCIS exercises its discretion to excuse the lapse in status.
Article Summary: Anthony D’Esposito, Inspector General at the Department of Labour has launched a sweeping investigation into fraud within the H-1B visa program. He has described the program as a ‘criminal enterprise’ which stretches beyond the borders of the US. He also said that the criminal networks are selling the white-collar jobs of Americans through the program which now keeps at least 1 million foreign workers.

Article Title: I-day security: Border and aerial surveillance in focus at Delhi railway hubs
Article Text:
Security has been heightened at Delhi's key railway transit hubs and surrounding areas

Eyes on Red Fort





NEW DELHI: In light of intelligence reports indicating potential threats to railway infrastructure, security measures have been intensified at key transit hubs and surrounding areas in the city.Fresh intelligence indicates Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) may have tasked Delhi-based assets to conduct immediate reconnaissance of key railway infrastructure in the capital.The threat adds to an alert sounded in connection with a message floated on Signal application by terror ideologue Farhatullah Ghori inciting Indian Muslims to join the ‘Army of Mahdi’, raise the banner of Islam over the national capital, and carry out sabotage and suicide attacks on ‘infidels’ and their families.There has been a series of critical security inputs gathered over recent weeks pointing to a coordinated push by cross-border outfits. Intelligence received on Aug 11 indicated that a Pakistan-based entity, operating with ties to ISI and pro-Khalistan elements like Babbar Khalsa International (BKI), was planning to deliver an IED to unknown associates in NCR within the next few days.Similarly, a May 25 communication to the National Investigation Agency (NIA) control room warned ISI was plotting six major blasts across India, with eight operatives linked to Talha Saeed having already entered the country.Earlier in May, intelligence agencies flagged plans by ISI to leverage established criminal and gangster networks to launch strikes on high-value buildings and infrastructure in Delhi.Additional alerts dating back to April and Feb pointed to Pakistan- and PoK-based terror groups targeting Delhi, Jammu, Rajasthan and the Parliament, as well as Lashkar-e-Taiba plans for IED blasts.Concurrently, Jaish-e-Mohammed has been actively luring youth through a social media handle named ‘Islah-e-Ummat’ to incite attacks on prominent dignitaries and key installations.Security has been significantly stepped up following revelations that terror modules operated by Pakistan-based gangster-terrorist Shehzad Bhatti had installed clandestine CCTV networks around major railway stations to monitor troop movements and security deployments.In light of these surveillance attempts, cops said they had swept railway premises, deployed extra quick response teams and placed armed personnel on round-the-clock vigil across all major transit hubs in the capital.All strategic border entry points into Delhi are set to be sealed by Thursday night, with intensive vehicle checking and verification drives underway.Security agencies have placed a special focus on counter-drone measures and aerial surveillance to thwart any low-altitude aerial threats over sensitive installations.Meanwhile, the number of rooftops where security personnel are being deployed has increased from 268 last year to 338 this year. As part of the security arrangements, police will also deploy body-worn cameras for personnel on the ground.
Article Summary: Security measures have been intensified at key transit hubs and surrounding areas in the city. Fresh intelligence indicates Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) may have tasked Delhi-based assets to conduct immediate reconnaissance of key railway infrastructure in the capital.

Article Title: Police say several bids were made to kill farmer in Kanjhawala
Article Text: New Delhi: Five men, multiple failed attempts and a 22-year-old revenge plot are what culminated in the murder of a farmer in northwest Delhi’s Kanjhawala.Police said the murder of Deepak Dabas — he was crushed under an SUV — was part of a conspiracy. Police have arrested all five accused in the case, including the alleged main conspirator, Pawan alias Jagpal Dabas (45), Wednesday. The conspiracy to kill Deepak took root 22 years ago after he allegedly molested Jagpal’s sister.DCP (Rohini) Shashank Jaiswal said: “Deepak, a farmer in Majra Dabas village, was killed on July 16 after a Scorpio SUV rammed into his scooter near Chandpur Majra Road in Kanjhawala. Initially, the case was registered as a fatal road accident. However, his family suspected foul play, prompting a detailed probe by a joint team of Kanjhawala police and the Rohini district special staff.”Police uncovered several earlier attempts to kill Deepak. They said that in Feb, someone opened fire outside Deepak’s brother’s home. On July 2, a Hyundai i10 rammed into Deepak’s scooter in Majra Dabas. Deepak’s 14-year-old son was with him at the time.Police got a breakthrough after the arrest of Sagar Kala (30) on July 17. Sagar allegedly admitted that the July 2 collision had been planned to kill Deepak. Police have found the Scorpio allegedly used on July 16 as well as the Hyundai i10 from co-accused Atul (30), who was also arrested.Investigators also arrested Sahil (23) for allegedly harbouring Jagpal and attempting to destroy evidence. Prince alias Tilli (24) was arrested for allegedly arranging for the SUV.
Article Summary: Police said the murder of Deepak Dabas — he was crushed under an SUV — was part of a conspiracy. The conspiracy to kill Deepak took root 22 years ago after he allegedly molested Jagpal’s sister. Police have arrested all five accused in the case, including the alleged main conspirator.

Article Title: Mumbai man gets 10-year jail term for stabbing woman over rejected proposal, attacking cop
Article Text:
The court relied on the deposition of the woman, her mother, the injured police constable, medical officers and panch witnesses





Mumbai: Noting that the rising incidents of attacks on police personnel and violence against girls arising from one-sided love are deeply concerning, over four years after a brutal knife attack on a woman and an intervening police constable, a sessions court on Thursday convicted and sentenced a 36-year-old salesman to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment for attempt to murder. The accused, Anil Babar, was upset as the woman had rejected his marriage proposal. “Such acts reflect a dangerous disregard for law, consent and human dignity. Strict legal action, timely intervention and greater awareness are essential to prevent such incidents and ensure the safety of both police personnel and women,” additional sessions judge RS Aradhye said.The judge also sentenced Babar to three years for stalking, five years for voluntarily causing grievous hurt to a public servant, one year for assaulting a public servant, two years for criminal intimidation and six months’ simple imprisonment under the Maharashtra Police Act. All sentences will run concurrently. “Even if for the sake of argument, it is accepted that there is a love affair between the victim and the accused, but that does not give any right or authority to the accused to assault the victim or any other person for the fulfillment of his proposal of marriage,” the judge said.The prosecution said Babar and the woman lived in the same locality at Salt Pan Road in Wadala East. According to the court record, Babar had developed “one-sided affection” for the woman and repeatedly proposed marriage, but the woman rejected the proposal.The crime occurred on the morning of May 4, 2022. Babar had been stalking the victim and continuously pressuring the victim for marriage despite previous police complaints. Around 10.30 am, the woman left home for work but forgot her mobile phone. Her mother followed to hand on the phone and saw Babar allegedly trying to stop the woman near Barkat Ali Bus Stop and Pooja Junction. When the victim refused to speak with the attacker, Babar pulled out a knife concealed in a waistband and inflicted severe stab wounds to the victim’s abdomen, back and arm. Police Constable Mayur Patil, who was on duty nearby, rushed to the scene to stop the assault. During the rescue attempt, Babar attacked the constable, severely slashing the officer’s hand. Other police personnel eventually disarmed Babar by striking the attacker’s hand with a wooden stick. Both the victim and the constable required prolonged hospitalisation and surgery.The woman was taken to KEM Hospital, where she remained admitted for 10 days and underwent surgery. Patil was treated at Wockhardt Hospital.The court relied on the deposition of the woman, her mother, the injured police constable, medical officers and panch witnesses.On the charge of attempt to murder, the court observed that the absence of fatal injury was not decisive. “The essentials are knowledge and intention of accused while committing the crime and if death were caused by that specific act,” the judge said.The court also held that the attack on the police constable was proved through the bandobast duty order and medical evidence. The judgement said the order showing Patil’s deployment at Kadaria Trust Mosque, Barkat Ali Nagar, Pooja Junction, was “more than sufficient for holding that…Patil was, on the day of incident at the relevant time discharging his duty as a public servant.”Before sentencing, public prosecutor Ranjana Budhwant sought maximum punishment, saying the offence arose out of a one-sided love affair and was also directed against police machinery.“This is the grave offence which the accused committed in the depression of failure in a love affair and brutally attacked the victim, as well as not leaving the Police Constable who tried to intervene in the matter. Therefore, taking into consideration the above-said facts and mitigating circumstances against the accused, I am of the view that in such a matter, if a lenient view is taken, it goes wrong message in society so the severe punishment provided for each offence will meet the ends of justice,” the judge said.Babar has been in custody since the day of the incident. The court directed that set-off be given for the period already spent in jail.
Article Summary: Anil Babar, 36, was sentenced to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment for attempt to murder. He was upset as the woman had rejected his marriage proposal. The court relied on the deposition of the woman, her mother, the injured police constable, medical officers and panch witnesses.

Article Title: State in Bombay high court: How can IMA challenge law permitting homeopaths to practise allopathy?
Article Text: Mumbai: State govt on Thursday questioned the Indian Medical Association’s legal right to challenge amendments to two Acts that introduced the Certificate Course in Modern Pharmacology (CCMP) and allowed homeopaths to practise allopathy.“How are they aggrieved by this Act?” asked advocate general Milind Sathe, arguing before a special bench of Justices Riyaz Chagla and Farhan Dubash. The 2014 amendments were made to Maharashtra Medical Council Act and Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act.Sathe argued that IMA is a “voluntary” association of doctors and has failed to show how it has suffered any “legal” injury because of the amendments. He said IMA cannot challenge the constitutional validity of a law merely on the ground that it disagrees with its provisions. He said it must demonstrate its locus standi and legal injury before asking HC to examine the validity of the legislation.Sathe also argued that IMA’s challenge is not based on any alleged violation of the fundamental right of doctors to practise their profession. “Is it the case (of the petitioner) their practice is being affected?” he asked. He also pointed out there was no challenge to the amendments based on Article 19 (1) (g) which protects the right to profession.Instead, IMA had questioned the state’s legislative competence to make amendments to both Acts. Sathe urged HC not to decide the validity of a law in a vacuum, “when the petitioner itself has not shown how it is affected by it.”IMA has challenged the legal framework permitting CCMP practitioners to practise allopathy. The state replied that the Maharashtra law creates a separate state-level registration regime and the provisions have existed as part of the state legislation since 1965. Also, Indian Medical Council Act regulates recognised qualifications for modern medicine at the Central level, while registration to practise in Maharashtra is governed by the state law.In Sept 2025, HC refused to stay registrations of CCMP practitioners, while making them subject to the final outcome of the main petition. It had also directed CCMP practitioners not to exceed their prescribed competency and to refer serious cases to fully qualified allopathy doctors. The arguments will continue on Friday.
Article Summary: State govt questions Indian Medical Association’s legal right to challenge amendments to two Acts. The 2014 amendments were made to Maharashtra Medical Council Act and Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act. They introduced Certificate Course in Modern Pharmacology (CCMP) and allowed homeopaths to practise allopathy.

Article Title: Dahanu bridge project stalled due to lack of funds, says zilla parishad after TOI report on family carrying body across swollen river to cremation ground
Article Text:
flood water

Dahanu

:





A day after TOI’s report on how a family in Dahanu taluka was forced to wade through a flooded river to complete the last rites of a relative due to the absence of a bridge, the district administration swung into action with a zilla parishad team inspecting the site on Thursday.Officials from the zilla parishad’s construction department said a bridge has already been proposed at the site, but the Rs 1-crore project has been stalled due to lack of funds. They added that efforts would be made to secure the required funds and take the project forward.Around 150 families live in Dhodipada in Dhundalwadi, Dahanu taluka. Although a gravel road leads to the local cremation ground, residents have to take a detour of around 1.5km to reach it. Villagers have been demanding a bridge over the river to provide a shorter and safer route, particularly for carrying bodies to the cremation ground.The issue came to the fore on Tuesday after a member of the Mukane family died and relatives were forced to carry the body through the flooded river to reach the cremation ground.
Article Summary: A family in Dahanu taluka was forced to wade through a flooded river to complete the last rites of a relative due to the absence of a bridge. The district administration swung into action with a zilla parishad team inspecting the site on Thursday. Around 150 families live in Dhodipada in Dhundalwadi, DahanU taluka.

Article Title: 'Kirpan aimed at his chest': Sukhbir Badal attacker shouted 'surrender' after bid failed; what we know
Article Text:
Sukhbir Singh Badal (L) narrowly escaped a kirpan attack at a gurdwara in Nanded

Who is Jaspal Singh?

Why did he attack Badal?

Second attack on Badal in less than two years

Political significance





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president and former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal escaped a potentially fatal attack at a gurdwara in Nanded on Thursday after a 62-year-old sevadar allegedly concealed a kirpan in a handkerchief and tried to strike him in the chest.Badal managed to evade the blow, taking the strike on his right forearm.The attack took place around 2pm at Mata Sahib Devaji Gurdwara in Mudkhed taluka, where Badal had gone with his wife and SAD MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal after offering prayers at Sachkhand Gurdwara. As Badal descended the steps after darshan, the accused, identified as Jaspal Singh Teja Singh Aidal of Pune, allegedly approached him with folded hands before suddenly pulling out the concealed kirpan.Former Nanded Gurdwara Board secretary Ravinder Singh Bungai, an eyewitness, said Jaspal had been standing with a large handkerchief in his hand, concealing the kirpan. When Badal approached him, the accused allegedly attempted to strike him in the chest. Badal managed to evade the blow and the weapon struck his arm instead.Security personnel immediately overpowered the attacker, preventing a more serious assault.Inspector Santosh Kendre of the Special Protection Unit (SPU), Nanded, was injured on his right forearm while intervening and securing the weapon.Badal was rushed to Yashosai Hospital in Nanded, where doctors confirmed a fracture. He was later reported to be stable and out of danger.Nanded superintendent of police Nilabh Rohan said security personnel acted swiftly to prevent a further attack. He said the accused was a 62-year-old Nihang Sikh and sevadar associated with the gurdwara.Jaspal was immediately arrested. Police said he had been staying at the Nanded gurdwara for the past two years and was working there as a sevadar.Bungai said the accused began shouting “surrendered, surrendered” after being restrained by police and security personnel.Jaspal Singh Teja Singh Aidal, 62, has deep roots in Pune and spent most of his life in the city's Camp area before moving to Nanded around two years ago for religious service, according to a crime branch officer.A law graduate, Jaspal tried several professions in Pune. Police inquiries found that he practised law for some time, ran a small newspaper and operated a snack centre in Camp for around three years before shutting it down.His wife, a schoolteacher, continues to live in the family's first-floor flat in Pune with their nephew. The Pune crime branch questioned his family members to establish his background and understand his activities.“His wife and others told us that he hardly contacted his family members,” DCP (crime) Gauhar Hassan said.A Maharashtra ATS team later visited Jaspal's home and conducted a search that continued until late at night. Nothing suspicious had been found at the residence until the time of reporting.A senior Maharashtra ATS officer said Jaspal initially gave evasive replies during questioning before claiming that he was angry over the drug menace in Punjab and held the Badal family responsible for it.Investigators are examining whether this was his actual motive or whether the attack had wider links or was part of a larger conspiracy.An FIR has been registered at Mudkhed police station under attempt-to-murder charges and relevant provisions of the Arms Act. Maharashtra ATS and central agencies have joined the investigation.Investigators are examining CCTV footage, the security deployment around Badal and the response of security personnel. They are also looking into how Jaspal managed to get close to Badal despite his security cover.Thursday's incident was the second attack on Badal in less than two years. In December 2024, he escaped unhurt after a man opened fire near the Golden Temple complex.Badal has Z-plus category security. However, he is entitled to CISF cover only in Punjab and Delhi, with around 40 personnel deployed. Punjab Police personnel were accompanying him when Thursday's attack took place.The attack comes barely a week after Badal's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, which had fuelled speculation about a possible BJP-SAD rapprochement ahead of the Punjab assembly elections.SAD leaders termed the attack a conspiracy to eliminate Badal and demanded a CBI inquiry.The incident also triggered an immediate response from the Maharashtra government. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis spoke to Badal, sought details from district police and ordered a high-level probe. Director general of police Sadanand Date and additional DGP (law and order) Nikhil Gupta also sought detailed reports.Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to Harsimrat Kaur Badal over the phone and enquired about Sukhbir Badal's health.The investigation is now focused on establishing Jaspal's motive, how he gained access to Badal and whether anyone else was involved in planning or facilitating the attack.
Article Summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal escaped a potentially fatal attack at a gurdwara in Nanded. A 62-year-old sevadar allegedly concealed a kirpan in a handkerchief and tried to strike him in the chest. Badal managed to evade the blow and the weapon struck his arm instead.

Article Title: SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal attacked at Nanded gurdwara; assailant arrested
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

Former deputy chief minister of Punjab Sukhbir Singh Badal rushes to a hospital after being attacked at a gurdwara, in Nanded, on Thursday

Former deputy chief minister of Punjab Sukhbir Singh Badal rushes to a hospital after being attacked at a gurdwara, in Nanded, on Thursday

Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president and former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal was injured after being attacked by a kirpan-wielding assailant while leaving the Mata Sahib Devaji Gurdwara at Mudkhed in Nanded district on Thursday, triggering a political storm and a multi-agency probe.The attack assumes political significance as it comes barely a week after Badal’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, which had fuelled speculation of a possible BJP-SAD rapprochement ahead of the Punjab assembly elections. Around 2pm, as he was descending the steps after darshan, the attacker allegedly struck at him with a concealed kirpan. Badal managed to deflect the blow, but suffered an injury to his right forearm. Security personnel intervened before a more serious assault could take place.Badal was immediately taken to Yashosai Hospital in Nanded, where doctors confirmed a fracture. He is said to be stable and out of danger. Inspector Santosh Kendre, of the Special Protection Unit (SPU) in Nanded, was also injured while intervening.The accused, identified as Jaspal Singh Teja Singh Aidal, a 62-year-old from Pune, was immediately overpowered and arrested. The police said he had been staying at the Nanded gurdwara for the last two years and was working there as a sevadar.Nanded superintendent of police Nilabh Rohan said security personnel acted swiftly to prevent a more serious attack.“The attacker, a 62-year-old, is a Nihang Sikh and sevadar associated with the gurdwara. He suddenly took out his kirpan to attack Badal. Security personnel, including Nanded police officers, immediately intervened and overpowered him, preventing any further attack. Inspector Santosh Kendre, posted with the SPU, Nanded, sustained an injury to his right forearm while overpowering the attacker and securing the weapon. ”An eyewitness account provided more details about how the attack unfolded. “After offering prayers at Sachkhand Gurdwara, Badal and his family went to Mata Sahib Gurdwara in Mudkhed taluka on Thursday afternoon. They offered prayers and came down the steps. Jaspal Singh was standing there with folded hands. He was carrying a large handkerchief in his hand and had concealed a kirpan inside it. As he was standing with folded hands, Sukhbir Singh approached him. The attacker then attempted to strike Badal in the chest with the kirpan. However, Badal managed to evade the blow and took the strike on his arm,” said Ravinder Singh Bungai, former secretary of the Nanded Gurdwara Board.Bungai said the accused began shouting “surrendered, surrendered” after being restrained by the police and security personnel.The attack is the second on Badal in less than two years. In Dec 2024, he escaped unhurt after firing near the Golden Temple complex. He is protected by Z-plus category security. However, he is entitled to CISF cover only in Punjab and Delhi, with a deployment of around 40 personnel. Punjab Police personnel were with him when the attack took place.An FIR has been registered at the Mudkhed police station under charges of attempt to murder and relevant provisions of the Arms Act. Maharashtra ATS and central agencies have joined the investigation.A senior ATS officer said the accused initially gave evasive replies during questioning before claiming he was angry over the drug menace in Punjab and held the Badal family responsible for it. Investigators, however, are examining whether there are wider links or a larger conspiracy behind the attack.“In addition to the ongoing probe, the DG office as well as the central agencies are also scrutinising how the assailant gained proximity to Badal, besides examining CCTV footage, security deployment and the response of security personnel,” an ATS officer said.The incident drew immediate attention at the highest political levels. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis spoke to Badal, sought details from district police and ordered a high-level probe. Director general of police Sadanand Date and additional DGP (law and order) Nikhil Gupta have sought a detailed report.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also spoke to Harsimrat Kaur Badal on the phone and enquired about Badal’s health after the attack.
Article Summary: Former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal was injured after being attacked by a kirpan-wielding assailant while leaving the Mata Sahib Devaji Gurdwara at Mudkhed in Nanded district.
